articles.title: Half-price rail travel extended to 18-year-olds
articles.summary: They'll be able to buy the 16-17 Saver railcard up until the day before they turn 18.
articles.content:
Eighteen-year-olds will be able to buy half-price train tickets for most services when railcard rules are changed later this month, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

It's an extension of the 16-17 Saver railcard which currently expires when the holder turns 18. From 17 August, they will be valid for a full year from the date of purchase.

It means 17-year-olds will be able to buy the railcard up until the day before they turn 18, making it valid until the day before they turn 19.

The existing rule meant more than 70,000 students each year were an average of £175 worse off than those in the same academic year who hadn't yet had their 18th birthday, the DfT said.

The 16-17 Saver Railcard costs £35 per year and entitles the holder to 50% off most train fares.

Rail minister Lord Hendy claimed this "common sense change" is "exactly what passengers should expect from the railway".

He said the change would "lower the cost of travel at a critical time for teenagers, whether they're pursuing further education, vocational pathways or getting their footing in the jobs market".

Jacqueline Starr, chief executive of industry body the Rail Delivery Group, said the change demonstrates the sector's commitment to "offering better value fares and delivering a more joined-up railway".

Kaynat Ahmad, vice president for further education at the National Union of Students, described the railcard as "essential for young people reliant on trains to get to college, work or training".

Eighteen-year-olds were already entitled to a 16-25 Railcard, but that only entitles them to a third off the cost of travel.

The announcement comes after the government said the cap on most single bus fares in England will be cut from £3 to £2 next year.

This policy change has a meaningful positive impact on accessibility and economic opportunity for youth, supported by clear details and official statements.
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Until now, young people could buy a special railcard that gives half-price train tickets only until they turned 18. This railcard, called the 16-17 Saver, helped many students save money on train travel.

**What happened** – Starting August 17, 17-year-olds can buy the 16-17 Saver railcard up until the day before they turn 18. This means the railcard will be valid for a full year from the purchase date, allowing 18-year-olds to keep using it until they turn 19. The railcard costs £35 and gives 50% off most train fares.

**Impact** – This change means over 70,000 young people each year will save around £175 on train travel compared to before. It helps students and young workers who rely on trains to get to school, college, or jobs. The discount is better than the 16-25 Railcard, which only offers a 33% discount for 18-year-olds.

**What's next step** – The government is also planning to reduce bus fares in England from £3 to £2 next year, making travel even more affordable for young people. The new railcard rules start later this month, and young people can begin buying the extended railcard right away.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Extending half-price train tickets to 18-year-olds makes travel cheaper and easier for young people continuing education or starting work.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les billets de train à moitié prix étendus aux jeunes de 18 ans
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Jusqu'à présent, les jeunes pouvaient acheter une carte de train spéciale à moitié prix seulement jusqu'à leurs 18 ans. Cette carte, appelée 16-17 Saver, aidait beaucoup d'étudiants à économiser sur leurs trajets en train.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – À partir du 17 août, les jeunes de 17 ans pourront acheter la carte 16-17 Saver jusqu'à la veille de leurs 18 ans. Cela signifie que la carte sera valable un an à partir de la date d'achat, permettant aux 18 ans de l'utiliser jusqu'à leurs 19 ans. La carte coûte 35 £ et donne 50 % de réduction sur la plupart des billets de train.

**Impact** – Ce changement permettra à plus de 70 000 jeunes chaque année d'économiser environ 175 £ sur leurs voyages en train par rapport à avant. Cela aide les étudiants et les jeunes travailleurs qui utilisent le train pour aller à l'école, au collège ou au travail. La réduction est meilleure que celle de la carte 16-25, qui offre seulement 33 % de réduction aux 18 ans.

**Prochaine étape** – Le gouvernement prévoit aussi de réduire le prix des bus en Angleterre de 3 £ à 2 £ l'année prochaine, rendant les déplacements encore plus abordables pour les jeunes. Les nouvelles règles pour la carte de train commencent ce mois-ci, et les jeunes peuvent dès maintenant en profiter.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Étendre les billets de train à moitié prix aux jeunes de 18 ans rend les déplacements moins chers et plus accessibles pour ceux qui poursuivent leurs études ou commencent à travailler.
articles.personality_title_es: Viajes en tren a mitad de precio extendidos a jóvenes de 18 años
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Hasta ahora, los jóvenes podían comprar una tarjeta especial para tren con mitad de precio solo hasta que cumplían 18 años. Esta tarjeta, llamada 16-17 Saver, ayudaba a muchos estudiantes a ahorrar en sus viajes en tren.

**Qué pasó** – Desde el 17 de agosto, los jóvenes de 17 años podrán comprar la tarjeta 16-17 Saver hasta el día antes de cumplir 18 años. Esto significa que la tarjeta será válida por un año completo desde la fecha de compra, permitiendo que los de 18 años la usen hasta que cumplan 19. La tarjeta cuesta £35 y ofrece un 50 % de descuento en la mayoría de los billetes de tren.

**Impacto** – Este cambio hará que más de 70,000 jóvenes cada año ahorren alrededor de £175 en viajes en tren comparado con antes. Ayuda a estudiantes y jóvenes trabajadores que dependen del tren para ir a la escuela, universidad o trabajo. El descuento es mejor que el de la tarjeta 16-25, que solo da un 33 % para los de 18 años.

**Próximo paso** – El gobierno también planea bajar el precio de los autobuses en Inglaterra de £3 a £2 el próximo año, haciendo el transporte aún más accesible para los jóvenes. Las nuevas reglas para la tarjeta de tren empiezan este mes, y los jóvenes pueden comprarla ya.

**Frase clave** – Extender el descuento del 50 % en trenes a los jóvenes de 18 años hace que viajar sea más barato y sencillo para quienes siguen estudiando o empiezan a trabajar.
